sections.h2: Who sends the property tax bill in Oldham County, Kentucky?
sections.html:
The Oldham County Sheriff's office sends and collects the bill, while the Property Valuation Administration (PVA) decides what the property is worth. The sheriff's tax page says the office collects for the state, the county, the school districts and the city of Crestwood, along with 18 special districts, and that bills are mailed by the end of September. The sheriff's number is 502-222-9501.

A bill that looks wrong goes to the PVA at 502-222-9320, because the sheriff never assesses value. The bill itself explains when payment is due, how to avoid penalties and what to do if a mortgage company pays on your behalf.

sections.h2: Why is Oldham County different from most Kentucky counties?
sections.html:
Oldham County sits in north central Kentucky inside the Louisville metropolitan area, and it is the wealthiest and best-educated county in the state according to Wikipedia's county profile. It covers 196 square miles, making it the 13th-smallest in Kentucky, with the Ohio River forming its northern line against Indiana.

The county was created in 1823 from parts of Henry, Jefferson and Shelby counties. Rail service in the 1850s spurred new towns, and Interstate 71, finished in the early 1970s, tied La Grange and the surrounding communities to downtown Louisville and turned the county into a suburban neighbor of the city's East End. The incorporated places include La Grange (the county seat), Crestwood, Goshen, Pewee Valley, Prospect, Orchard Grass Hills and River Bluff, with Buckner and Westport as census-designated places.

Oldham County Schools operates North Oldham High School, Oldham County High School and South Oldham High School, and the school an address feeds is often the first question a buyer asks.

sections.h2: How do payment deadlines work for Oldham County owners?
sections.html:
State law sets one calendar for every sheriff. Under KRS 134.015, paying in full by November 1 earns a 2 percent discount, the face amount is due through December 31, and a 5 percent penalty applies in January, rising to 10 percent afterward.

  • Owners who have an escrow account with a lender should confirm the lender paid before the discount date.
  • A buyer who closes in the fall should have the title agent confirm who pays the current bill.
  • A bill for a parcel in Crestwood includes the city's levy as well as the county's.

Because the bill follows the owner on January 1, a seller who closes in spring still receives the year's bill and settles it with the buyer at closing.

sections.h2: How can an Oldham County owner dispute an assessment?
sections.html:
Call the PVA first and ask for a conference. The state process, summarized in a PVA appeal guide, treats this as the required first step. Owners are asked to name their own opinion of value and back it up with comparable sales, an appraisal, repair quotes or a rental income record.

If that fails, an appeal form is filed with the County Clerk by the day after the inspection period closes. A local board of three residents hears it, and the Kentucky Board of Tax Appeals handles the next level, with 30 days from the mailed ruling to file.

sections.h2: What happens to unpaid Oldham County taxes?
sections.html:
Unpaid bills move from the sheriff to the County Clerk after the close of business on April 15. The Oldham County Clerk's delinquent tax page sends owners back to the PVA for valuation questions and to the Department of Revenue for information on the state's tax sales.

The state's collection guide says a lien is recorded, interest of 1 percent a month runs, and the county attorney sends notices before a sale that cannot be held sooner than 90 days after the transfer. After a sale, a private buyer holds the lien and the owner pays that buyer. A seller with a certificate on the parcel should settle it at closing from the sale proceeds, and the clerk can provide the payoff.

sections.h2: What should an Oldham County seller expect at closing?
sections.html:
The state's transfer tax is 50 cents for each $500 of value or fraction, billed to the seller and collected by the clerk with the deed (KRS 142.050). On a $393,100 sale that is 787 units, or $393.50. Transfers between spouses, to correct an earlier deed or under foreclosure are exempt.

  • The deed must state the full price, both mailing addresses and an in-care-of address for the next bill.
  • A gift or a sale for nominal money needs a sworn statement of the estimated market value.
  • Heirs must file the personal representative's affidavit with the clerk of each county where the estate owns land.

sections.h2: What is moving the Oldham County market?
sections.html:
Growth is steady. Oldham County added about 3,400 residents between April 2020 and July 2025, and builders recorded 276 permits in 2025. Almost half of adults 25 or older hold a bachelor's degree (46.4 percent), and 95.4 percent of households have broadband, which helps remote work. Mean commute time is 26.2 minutes.

Those figures describe a county tied closely to the Louisville job market, and the spread of places from La Grange to Pewee Valley, Crestwood and Goshen means two houses a few miles apart can fall in different tax districts. Ask the sheriff which districts are on a given bill.

faqs.q: Who do I call if my Oldham County tax bill seems too high?
faqs.a: Call the Oldham County PVA at 502-222-9320. The sheriff's office collects the bill but never sets the value.

faqs.q: When are Oldham County tax bills mailed?
faqs.a: By the end of September, according to the sheriff's tax page. Owners who have not received one by early October should call the sheriff at 502-222-9501 for a copy.

faqs.q: Does Crestwood collect its own property tax?
faqs.a: No. The sheriff collects Crestwood's tax along with the county and district levies, so the owner pays one office.

faqs.q: What is the Kentucky transfer tax on a median-priced Oldham County home?
faqs.a: $393.50 on a $393,100 sale. The seller owes 50 cents per $500 of value or fraction, and the clerk collects it when the deed is recorded.

faqs.q: Can I sell an Oldham County house that has a delinquent tax lien?
faqs.a: Yes. The lien is paid from the sale proceeds at closing, and the County Clerk can give the title company a payoff figure good through a stated date.
